finding.summary: Timestamp ordering alone does not prove that both independent enumerations completed before stabilization snapshots began, or that the two client executions and snapshots occurred within bounded windows.
finding.uncertainty: The gate proves only declared timestamp relationships; it does not authenticate clocks, prove repository quiescence, or prove provider consistency.

primary_sources.title: GitHub REST API endpoints for workflow runs
observed: head_sha filters workflow runs to the specified commit
filtered searches can return at most 1000 results
private-repository access requires authenticated Actions read permission

primary_sources.title: GitHub CLI gh api manual
observed: --slurp combines paginated JSON responses into an outer array

verification.environment: isolated Node runtime using byte-identical implementation and test content before commit
verified_cases: stabilization before both executions complete rejected
invalid or unbounded policy window rejected

falsification_route: Provide a case where both executions and snapshots satisfy the gate but retained bytes prove they came from different repository or commit identities.
Demonstrate that declared timestamps were produced by unsynchronized or manipulated clocks.
Show repository mutation between snapshots despite a passing bounded observation window.
design_implication: Run the observation-window gate after execution identity, retained-byte binding, and temporal-coherence validation, but before reconciliation evidence is promoted. A passing result must remain a bounded ordering claim, not a quiescence or authenticity claim.
